explain.say: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes exactly between the Sun and Earth, at new moon. Its shadow falls on Earth, and anyone inside the darkest part sees a total eclipse.

explain.say: Over about an hour the Moon slides across the Sun, taking a bigger and bigger bite. As the last sliver goes, the daylight turns eerie, the air cools, and birds may fall silent.

explain.say: At totality the Sun's bright face is completely hidden. Stars and planets appear, and the Sun's faint outer atmosphere, the corona, glows around the black Moon. It lasts at most about seven and a half minutes.

faq.q: Why can the small Moon cover the huge Sun?
faq.a: The Sun is about 400 times wider than the Moon, but it is also about 400 times further away. So from Earth they look almost exactly the same size in the sky.
asks: How can the Moon block out the Sun?

faq.a: The corona is the Sun's thin outer atmosphere, over a million degrees but very faint. It is normally hidden by the Sun's glare and shows up as pearly streamers only during a total eclipse.
asks: What is the glow around the Sun in an eclipse?

faq.q: Why must you never look at the Sun during an eclipse?
faq.a: Even a thin sliver of the Sun is bright enough to damage the back of your eye, without any pain to warn you. Use certified eclipse glasses or a pinhole projector; only during full totality is it safe to look directly.
asks: Is it safe to look at an eclipse?

faq.q: How rare is a total solar eclipse?
faq.a: Somewhere on Earth sees one roughly every 18 months, but the path of totality is narrow, rarely more than about 250 kilometres wide. Any one place waits on average about 375 years between total eclipses.
asks: How often do total solar eclipses happen?

faq.a: Just before and after totality, a last bead of sunlight shines through a valley on the Moon's edge, beside the thin glowing ring of the corona. It looks like a sparkling diamond ring.
asks: What is the diamond ring effect?

facts: The Sun is about 400 times wider than the Moon and about 400 times further away, so they look nearly the same size from Earth.
Totality in a solar eclipse can last at most about 7 minutes 32 seconds.
A solar eclipse can only happen at new moon.

quiz.say: At what phase of the Moon can a solar eclipse happen?
quiz.show: A solar eclipse can only happen at…
quiz.why: Only at new moon is the Moon between the Sun and Earth, where it can block the Sun.

wrong.0: At full moon the Moon is behind Earth; that is when lunar eclipses happen.
